title: The Undertow of the fourth floor walk-up
premise: Rosalind Ashgrove, once a celebrated piano prodigy who vanished from the conservatory at nineteen, returns two decades later not as a musician but as a janitor in the crumbling fourth-floor walk-up slated for demolition. When she hears an unrecorded song—her own composition, stolen and released by her former mentor—playing on a radio, she is forced to confront the life she abandoned, the lover she never chose, and the self she erased. As demolition day approaches, Rosalind pieces together old photographs and half-spoken truths, learning that survival cost her everything except the chance to forgive. In the end, she plays the unfinished song aloud in the empty building one last time, choosing love over duty at last—not to reclaim her past, but to finally let it go.
about_author: Wendell Dunmore is the pen name of a former conservatory custodian who spent fifteen years sweeping concert halls before turning to fiction. His work explores the quiet lives of people who almost became extraordinary.
